text:
Two progress figures for the same project, about ten points apart. Both were calculated correctly.

The progress report said 73%. The manhour budget said 63%, for the same work on the same date. I had to reconcile them, and nobody had made a mistake. Three things caused the gap:

1. Capped quantities. One system stops counting when a line reaches 100% of its BOQ quantity. Site keeps working, so earned work drops out of the figure.
2. Different weights. One weights each activity by its own manhours. The other spreads a standard rate over the quantity.
3. Scope outside the budget. Work measured on site that has no line in the manhour budget.

On the same basis, the two systems agreed to within 0.1 of a point.

Before you defend your number, check which of the three you are looking at.

Which one causes the most arguments on your project?
